dct_description_sm: The impacts of climate change are already being felt in aboriginal communities across Quebec. In maritime regions, coastal erosion is expected to result in significant costs in municipal infrastructure and damage to residential properties. A number of Micmac and Inuit live in proximity to the Gulf of Saint Lawrence and will be touched by these impacts. In southern Quebec, the frequency, magnitude, or duration of extreme weather events is also expected to increase as a result of climate change. Mohawk, Huron-Wendat, and Abenaki communities are located in this region. The purpose of the project aimed to: (1) acquire community-based perception of climate change; (2) respect and take into account traditional knowledge on the territory and compliment them with science; (3) raise awareness in communities on the importance of climate change and adaptation and; (4) determine the risks and vulnerabilities linked to climate change.
